description: Run or supervise one structured program/argv command. action=run is synchronous. For a long command, action=start returns a Runtime-owned handle only after policy, approval, and sandbox startup succeed; use action=status with bounded waitMs to long-poll it, or action=cancel to terminate its process tree. Manual and auto-approved modes use Runtime policy plus the Anthropic workspace sandbox. User-confirmed dangerous mode runs directly as the current OS user. Explicit one-shot shells remain supported, but detached shell processes are not.

propertyDescriptions.action: run waits for a command to finish; start returns a supervised handle; status observes or long-polls that handle; cancel terminates it. Legacy callers may omit action for synchronous run.
propertyDescriptions.program: Executable name or workspace-relative executable; absolute host executables require dangerous mode.
propertyDescriptions.args: The structured argument vector passed directly to the program. Never repeat program or its executable basename in args[0]; args starts with the first real argument.
propertyDescriptions.cwd: Workspace-relative existing directory, or an absolute host directory only in dangerous mode.
propertyDescriptions.intent: The purpose of the command, used by Runtime when applying execution policy.
propertyDescriptions.timeoutMs: An optional requested command-phase timeout. Runtime applies the minimum of this request, the configured command limit, and the classified capability limit, then returns all four timeout values including the effective limit.
propertyDescriptions.reason: A concise explanation of why this command is needed for the current task.
propertyDescriptions.commandId: The exact Runtime-issued command handle returned by action=start.
propertyDescriptions.waitMs: For action=status, wait up to this many milliseconds (maximum 30000) for a terminal result before returning a running snapshot.

guidance: run_command executes a structured program/argument-vector command under the active Runtime posture. Put the executable only in program; args[0] must be the first real argument, never program again. Use action=run for short commands. For long tests or builds, use action=start once, retain its commandId, then call action=status with waitMs up to 30000 until terminal; use action=cancel when the work is no longer needed. Started, running, and terminal results expose requestedMs, effectiveMs, configuredLimitMs, and capabilityLimitMs; effectiveMs is the command-phase timeout Runtime actually enforces. Never emulate supervision with nohup, disown, shell background &, Start-Job, Start-Process, cmd start /b, sleep, Start-Sleep, or timeout polling. Do not run file-mutation tools while a handle is running; Runtime retains the workspace mutation lease until actual process completion. Always reach a terminal status or cancel a handle before finishing the task. Prefer existing project scripts. An explicit one-shot shell may be requested with cmd /c, PowerShell -Command, or sh -c; never request an interactive, login, encoded, or detached shell. Outside Dangerous full access, Runtime independently classifies, approves, and sandboxes every process. If Runtime classifies the first sandbox_unavailable result as retryable and explicitly requests one bounded retry, retry exactly once and do not block a DAG for that transient failure. If Runtime then reports a turn-scoped sandbox pause, do not retry again; continue non-command work or return a concise pause report so the next turn can retry.
